units.text: INT. OPERA HOUSE INFIRMARY - EVENING
The stalls have been torn out and replaced with rows of iron cots.
Gilt cherubs look down over bandaged men.
Through a blown-out window, a wintry sky the color of ash.
SERGEANT BRONISLAW KRAJEWSKI (40s, thick moustache, arm in a sling) sits on the edge of a cot, mending a boot by lantern light.
LIEUTENANT SIPHO MBEKI (30s, upright, clean spectacles) writes a letter on a drum case.
NURSE FIONNUALA DOYLE (30s, red hair under a veil, sleeves rolled) kneels to change a dressing.
A small figure sits cross-legged on the stage, back to them, a boy in a coat too big, watching the dust fall through the light.
Nobody has asked him a thing.
That one has not spoken since the bridge.
units.name: KRAJEWSKI

units.text: Perhaps he has nothing to say.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: He ate. That is something.
units.name: DOYLE

units.text: It was mine.
units.name: THE BOY

units.text: They all stop.
The boy does not move.
Doyle stands.
What was yours, love?
units.name: DOYLE

units.text: The bread. You gave it to the other man. I only wanted to know why.
units.name: THE BOY

units.text: Krajewski lowers the boot.
Mbeki sets down his pen.
What is your name, young man?
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: Ilario.
units.name: THE BOY

units.text: Ilario. A good name. Mine is Sipho.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: What does it mean?
units.name: ILARIO

units.text: Gift.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: Ilario studies him.
His eyes are very old.
Then why does everyone here look as if they've lost one?
units.name: ILARIO

units.text: Doyle sits on the stage beside him.
Krajewski clears his throat, puts down the boot, and stands, one hand on his sling.
Ilario. Come, eat with us.
units.name: KRAJEWSKI

units.text: Ilario hesitates.
Then he rises and walks to the cot, small and dignified.
Krajewski tears the last of his own bread and hands him half.
Mbeki sets aside the letter and pours three cups of water.
